---
title: Online vocabulary
description: "Category, Set, and Cluster learn labels during training, grow storage automatically, and handle unknown values."
engine: markdown
---

`Category`, `Set`, and `Cluster` learn their labels from training data. Supply
merchant names and tags directly; there is no separate integer-encoding step.
Each field keeps its own vocabulary, saved with the model.

## A vocabulary belongs to a field

Extend the [transaction history](../learn/add-transaction-history.qmd) with
transaction tags. Earlier payments and the latest payment use the same field
definitions inside `trxns`:

```yaml
trxns:
  - booked_at: "2026-05-21T10:00:00"
    amount: 32.00
    merchant: Station Cafe
    tags:
      - food
      - cafe
    disputed: false
  - booked_at: "2026-05-27T18:15:00"
    amount: 56.20
    merchant: North Market
    tags:
      - grocery
      - in_store
    disputed: true
  - booked_at: "2026-05-28T14:30:00"
    amount: 84.50
    merchant: North Market
    tags:
      - grocery
      - in_store
    disputed: false
```

```python
import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model.xs(
    trxns=rf.Branch(
        length=32,
        overflow="tail",
        booked_at=rf.DateParts(
            dateparts=["day_of_month", "day_of_week", "hour_of_day"],
        ),
        amount=rf.Number,
        merchant=rf.Category,
        tags=rf.Set,
        disputed=rf.Boolean(mask=True),
    ),
)
```

Every transaction position uses `/trxns/merchant`. That field learns one
merchant vocabulary shared by the earlier and latest payments; both North
Market values use the same mapping. `/trxns/tags` owns a separate mapping,
shared across its transaction positions. There is no duplicate root merchant
field. [Preprocessing](../guides/preprocessing.qmd) covers preparing this
collection from application records.

Keep labels in one compatible Arrow type family and normalize spelling, case,
and label types upstream. A null is a separate value state and consumes no
vocabulary slot. Set members are labels; the entire set is not one vocabulary entry.

## When labels are learned

| Stage | Vocabulary behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Training | Admit new labels before the batch's forward pass, growing storage as needed. |
| Validation and test | Reuse the existing mapping; unseen labels remain unknown. |
| Prediction and serving | Reuse the loaded mapping; requests do not teach new labels. |
| Fine-tuning or resumed training | Continue from the saved mapping, admitting new labels and growing storage as needed. |

```{typst}

In the training lane, batch one carries Station Cafe and North Market and admits two labels; batch two carries North Market and Harbor Internet and admits one more label while existing IDs keep their rows. In the prediction lane, a request carrying North Market and Pier Bakery reuses the mapping without admission, and Pier Bakery is marked unavailable while remaining a valued input."
#flow(

    step("Admit 2 labels", kind: "root", note: "Rows allocated before the forward pass"),
    step("Batch 2", kind: "branch", note: "North Market, Harbor Internet"),
    step("Admit 1 label", kind: "root", note: "Storage grows; existing IDs keep their rows"),

  (title: "Prediction", steps: (
    step("Request", kind: "branch", note: "North Market, Pier Bakery"),
    step("Reuse the mapping", kind: "root", note: "No admission"),
    step("Pier Bakery unavailable", kind: "target", note: "Still a valued input, with no vocabulary row"),
  )),

```

Learning observes the pristine values retained by the schema, after
preprocessing and query/overflow selection but before input masking and
`p_unavailable` perturbations. An always-hidden Category target therefore
learns its label vocabulary too. Masking does not prevent vocabulary learning.

Admission does not move existing predictions: a newly admitted label embeds
exactly as it did while unknown, because its content row starts at zero, and
its decoder row starts silent until gradients move it. The next training
batch gives every still-zero content row a normal start before using it, so
labels become distinguishable as soon as learning resumes; outside training
the rows stay at zero and predictions hold.

Training-stage encoding, including `model.encode(..., strata="train")`, can
update this state even without an optimizer step. Validation or prediction on
a newly constructed model starts with empty vocabularies; load a trained
artifact to reuse its mappings.

## Inspect and reuse the mapping

After training the example model:

```python
merchant_address = rf.Address("trxns", "merchant")
merchant_labels = rf.Category.vocabulary(model, merchant_address)
merchant_counts = rf.Category.counts(model, merchant_address)
tag_labels = rf.Set.vocabulary(model, rf.Address("trxns", "tags"))
merchant_label_count = len(merchant_labels)
```

Vocabulary accessors return immutable tuples in slot order. Category counts
are pristine training exposures for populated labels, excluding the smoothing
prior and unavailable values. Repeated epochs count again; these are not
unique-record counts. DDP exposure counts synchronize at epoch end and before
the evaluation-loop warning checks.
New training labels are counted from their first consumed batch.
`rf.Cluster.vocabulary(model, address)` provides the same mapping inspection
for Cluster fields.

Preprocessors can inspect established mappings through `encoding_context`.
Training preprocessing runs before vocabulary admission: filtering new labels
against that snapshot would prevent them from being learned. Normalize labels
there, and reserve vocabulary-based filtering for an explicit application
policy. See [Preprocessing](../guides/preprocessing.qmd#scope-and-context).

[Save/load](../guides/checkpoints-ema-and-resuming.qmd#save-and-load) preserves the mapping and
associated model state. [Fine-tuning](../learn/pretraining-and-fine-tuning.qmd) continues
learning from it; freezing parameter gradients alone does not freeze vocabulary
admission. Use prediction stages for a fixed vocabulary.

Cluster also has an explicit [assignment API](../datatypes/cluster.qmd#learning-and-inspection)
that can add labels and grow storage on an idle model outside training.

Automatic growth needs no schema update. Resetting a field discards its learned
vocabulary and runtime state. Review [Schema mutation](../guides/schema-mutation.qmd)
before explicitly rebuilding a trained field.

## Unknown values and prediction

At evaluation, a label outside the learned mapping remains `valued`; it does
not become null.
Its content representation depends on the datatype:

| Type | Unknown content |
| --- | --- |
| Category | Zero categorical content plus the value-state embedding. |
| Set | Known membership plus unavailable-member counts. A learned unavailable contribution distinguishes unknown from empty sets, without recovering unknown identities. |
| Cluster | A shared unavailable assignment. |

These types default to `p_unavailable=0.01`, which simulates unavailable content
during training. All three perturb inputs only, preserving the original
reconstruction answers. This changes input content, not membership in the
learned vocabulary or pristine exposure counts. See the datatype pages for
their respective loss and coverage definitions: a Set counts memberships,
where Category and Cluster count scalar targets.

Predictions name only populated vocabulary entries. Category and Cluster label
probabilities are normalized over those entries; Set emits their independent
membership probabilities. None can name an unseen label. A high probability
does not establish that a request belongs to the known vocabulary. Evaluate
unknown-label coverage alongside content accuracy, which excludes unknown
targets for Category and Cluster.

### Cold input identities

Simulated unavailable inputs teach prediction from the context that
remains. They cannot teach the identity-specific effect of an unseen arbitrary
ID. A model can legitimately remain confident when other fields are decisive;
there is no universal OOV confidence cap. Use entity-disjoint or time-respecting
validation to assess the actual cold-start population, not just a stratified
row split. Evaluate proper scores such as NLL or Brier score separately for
known and unseen input groups.

`p_unavailable` is an explicit input-augmentation policy, not an estimate of
how often a category will be missing during inference. Increasing it can improve
the fallback while weakening use of known identity. Select it on a separate
development split; do not learn a vocabulary from validation to conceal OOVs.
[P061](../evidence/vocabulary/cold-start-confidence.py) measures both regimes and
includes decisive-context controls. Its synthetic missing-ID population does
not establish robustness to arbitrary new-population effects.

Vocabulary admission activates an unused or newly allocated representation.
For Category that representation starts where the unknown label stood: a zero
content row and a silent decoder row, so existing predictions are unchanged
until training moves it. Admission does not train the representation. Keep
serving vocabularies frozen, and evaluate a separately continued-training
artifact before promotion. Counts measure exposures, not representation competence.

At the start of each Lightning validation, test, or prediction loop, RelFlow
warns when any learned label has fewer than **10 training observations**.
The warning identifies the field and exposure counts without logging label
values. It changes neither predictions nor losses. This includes sanity
validation during fitting, but not direct `model.predict(payments)` calls.
Ten exposures are a diagnostic threshold, not a guarantee of learning.

[P066](../evidence/vocabulary/rolling-input-admission.py) measures how admitting
input labels changes reconstruction quality across successive training cohorts.
For pretraining targets, see
[coverage-aware evaluation](../learn/pretraining-and-fine-tuning.qmd#evaluate-vocabulary-coverage).

## Automatic storage growth

Category, Set, and Cluster manage vocabulary storage automatically. Neither
`size` nor `capacity` is a field option, and there is no configured maximum.
When a training batch introduces more labels than fit, storage grows
geometrically until it can hold them. Users do not need to estimate the number
of labels before training. Cluster's `bounds` controls latent clusters, not
vocabulary storage.

Growth preserves existing label IDs, learned embedding and decoder rows,
exposure counters, partial gradients, and optimizer history: Adam/AdamW moments
and step counters, or SGD momentum. New parameter rows receive standard
initialization and zeroed optimizer moments or momentum. Cluster preserves its unavailable assignment
while growing per-label rows; its configured cluster bounds are unchanged.
Checkpoints preserve the mapping and grown tensor sizes, so resumed training
can continue from that allocation. Vocabulary storage is runtime state, not
schema configuration; growing it does not change the schema.

Labels append in encounter order without evicting or renumbering existing ones.
With DDP, each batch's labels are gathered in rank order, preserving encounter
order within each rank. Record order, shuffling, and rank layout can change the
assigned IDs, but early rare labels do not exclude later common labels.
[P057](../evidence/vocabulary/capacity-admission-order.py) checks admission and
learning across encounter orders.

Automatic growth still consumes memory and increases decoder cost. In particular,
Set membership and decoder outputs span the current allocation. Spare rows are
not labels: reconstruction objectives and written probabilities use only
discovered labels. Actual new labels can change the learning objective;
additional storage alone does not add classes.

Use [Hash](../datatypes/hash.qmd) for identifier equality without a persistent
vocabulary. [Cluster](../datatypes/cluster.qmd) shares latent representations
between labels but still keeps growing per-label state.

## Workers and distributed training

Data workers encode immutable dictionaries local to each batch. The training
process binds those dictionaries to the model's current vocabulary before
forward, admits the new labels, and remaps inputs, targets, and exposure counts.
Prefetched batches remain valid across growth because their local IDs are
resolved when consumed. Labels are available to their first training batch,
including with multiple workers.

Under DDP, every rank gathers that batch's dictionaries and applies the same
ordered admission. When parameters grow, RelFlow replaces the DDP wrapper
during the current fit, before the affected batch enters forward, and migrates
optimizer state to the grown parameters.

Growth also happens before the affected batch during gradient accumulation
(`accumulate_grad_batches > 1`). Before replacing the DDP wrapper, RelFlow
synchronizes which parameters have gradients and their partial gradients across
ranks. Resizing preserves these gradients, including contributions from
parameters used only in earlier microbatches, and accumulation continues.

Automatic growth supports single-device training and standard eager Lightning
DDP with automatic optimization and `static_graph=False`; DDP growth during
accumulation requires dense gradients. FSDP, DeepSpeed, other sharded backends,
compiled DDP, and DDP configurations with native mixed precision, custom
communication hooks, or delayed all-reduce are unsupported for growth.

Checkpoints record the model's admitted vocabulary and allocated rows.
Prefetching alone does not admit labels or record training exposures. Integer
slots are local to a trained model; preserve its artifact and inspect its mapping
when reusing it.

The [Vocabulary and OOV evidence](../evidence.qmd)
exercise unknown inputs and targets, vocabulary growth, set membership, and
checkpoint/continued-training behavior. They distinguish learned fallback
from information that a frozen evaluation vocabulary cannot represent.
